meta.title: SMAT implementation-grade specification, extracted from the two SMAT PDFs for an independent reconstruction

O.id: arXiv:2603.07618v1 (8 Mar 2026), IROS 2026 to appear per E ref [14]

E.id: arXiv:2608.00715v1 (1 Aug 2026), submitted to IEEE (journal not named)

conventions: Locators: 'O pN' / 'E pN' = printed page of that PDF; Table/Fig/Eq numbers are as printed in THAT paper.

'not reported' = absent from both PDFs. 'derived' = our arithmetic or analysis from published equations/tables, not an author claim. 'read from Fig. N, approximate' = visual read of the rendered page, no digitisation.
'measured' vs 'argued': simulation numbers are author-reported outputs of their runs; causal explanations in the text are argued unless an ablation tests them.

Symbols: dt = 0.02 s; u_j = normalized exo command in [-1,1] (j in {l,r}); omega_j = hip flexion angular velocity (rad/s); w_j = omega_hat_j = clip(omega_j / 2.0, -1, 1); a_j = muscle activation in [0,1].

equation_map_O_to_E.PPO_table: O Table II = E Table S4 (identical)
equation_map_O_to_E.reward_weight_table: O Table I = E Table S2 (identical numbers, different footnote)
equation_map_O_to_E.hardware_table: O Table III (Pi 4B, encoders) vs E Table I (Pi 5, encoders or 3 IMUs)

simulator.name: MyoAssist (MuJoCo / MyoSuite-based musculoskeletal simulation)
simulator.citation: O ref [12] = E ref [19]: Tan et al., 'MyoAssist 0.1: MyoSuite for dexterity and agility in bionic humans', ICORR 2025
simulator.control_source: O p3 (text after Eq2; Algorithm 1 'Require: v* = 1.25 m/s, dt = 0.02 s (50 Hz), gamma = 0.99'); E p3
simulator.terrain: level ground only (E p8: 'trained on level ground only'); treadmill vs overground plane in simulation not reported
simulator.sensor_noise_in_sim: not reported; E p5: 'the policy was trained on unfiltered kinematics'
simulator.reward_time_scaling: every reward term is multiplied by dt so that 'the reward magnitude [is] independent of control frequency' (O p3; E p3)
simulator.episode_reward_scale_constraint_derived: Fig. 2 (O p5) episode reward plateaus near 6.5-7 in Stages 1 and 2 (read from Fig. 2, approximate). Max Stage-1 per-step reward from Table S2/S3 = 0.02*(0.8 + 1.85 + 1.89 + 0.005) = 0.091 (bilateral DOFs counted on both sides; r_muscle <= 0 ignored), so a ~6.5 plateau needs at least ~72 control steps per episode and more with realistic tracking error. This is a weak consistency check only; episode length is not reported.

body_model.source: O p1-2; E p2; E Fig. 2 caption p4 ('26-muscle musculoskeletal model used for training (13 muscles per side, red)')
body_model.muscles_named_source: O p3 (M_hip), O Fig. 4 p6, E p3 (M_hip), E Fig. 4 p6; E p9-10 also mentions 'several other distal muscles', so the 13 per side contain more distal muscles than gastrocnemius and soleus
body_model.dimensionality: 3D, inferred (not stated): E Table S3 tracks pelvis_tz, pelvis_list, pelvis_rotation, hip_adduction and hip_rotation, and the device has passive abduction joints
body_model.dofs_source: E Table S3 p14 (tracked DOFs; 18 DOFs if bilateral counted twice). Whether the model has further untracked DOFs (e.g., subtalar) is not reported.
body_model.human_body_mass_in_sim: not reported (r_constraint and r_foot normalise by body weight mg; which m is used is not reported)
body_model.activation_dynamics: not reported. O p2: actor 'directly outputs 26 muscle activations a in [0,1]^26 (13 per side)' and 'The policy directly controls muscle excitations'. E p2: '26 muscle excitations e in [0,1]^26'. Rewards use activation a_j (O p3; E p2-3).
body_model.joint_angle_conventions: not reported; read from Fig. 2 (O p5), approximate: knee plotted negative in flexion (0 to about -60 deg), hip about +25 to -15 deg, ankle about +10 to -20 deg over the gait cycle

device_model.components: pelvis-mounted frame and bilateral thigh links 'parented directly to the corresponding human body segments, coupling the device mass and inertia into the body dynamics' (O p3; E p3 'parented to the corresponding body segments')
device_model.actuation: assistance torques act coaxially at the human hip flexion joints (O p3); 'The exoskeleton actuators apply torque directly to the human hip flexion joints' (E p3)
device_model.passive_joints: passive abduction joints providing lateral compliance (O p3; E p3 refers to Fig. 2 hinge 4)
device_model.joint_axes: sagittal flexion/extension axis coaxial with the human hip flexion joint (O p3); on hardware the exo axis is aligned with the anatomical hip axis during fitting (O p4; E p4)
device_model.sim_mass_kg: not reported. Hardware total mass is 5.94 kg (O Table III p4; E Table I p4). Whether the simulated device uses 5.94 kg, and its split between pelvis frame and thigh links, is not reported.
device_model.sim_actuator_model: not reported beyond ideal torque at the human hip flexion joints: no motor inertia, friction, backdrive, delay, bandwidth or torque-speed limit is described
device_model.command_interface: normalized u in [-1,1]^2 (right, left) scaled by a stage-dependent torque limit tau_max (O p2; E p2)
device_model.torque_limit_source: O p3 (Stage 2: 'the exoskeleton actuator torque limit is set to zero in the simulation model, so no assistance torque is applied regardless of the actor output'); O Algorithm 1 lines 9, 15, 22 p3; E p3-4; E Algorithm S1 lines 6-7, 13, 20 p13
device_model.stage2_attach_wording: O Alg. 1 line 9: 'Attach exoskeleton structure (mass/inertia added); load pi_h(1); set exoskeleton torque to zero'. E Alg. S1 line 6: 'Attach the passive exoskeleton (mass/inertia only)'; line 7: 'Set exoskeleton torque tau = 0'.
device_model.passive_joint_implementation: not reported (with thigh links parented to the femur, an explicit abduction hinge is either redundant or needs an equality constraint)
device_model.sim_device_burden_reported: E p9-10: 'in simulation several hip muscles were less active at Stage 2 than at Stage 1'; gastrocnemius and several other distal muscles rose, soleus fell. The simulated device therefore did not raise hip-muscle activation, unlike the +13.1% human metabolic penalty (E p7).

control.hardware_timing: fixed 20 ms loop; torque command transmitted at the end of each cycle, controller idle until the next update (E p5), i.e., up to one control period between sensing and actuation; whether simulation models this delay is not reported
control.source: O p3 Algorithm 1; O Table II p4; E p4-5; E Table S4 p14

human_actor.inputs: 'a musculoskeletal body-state observation' (O p2; E p2). No list, dimension, ordering or normalisation is given anywhere. Fig. 1 (O p2; E p3) only shows 'Observation' going to the actors and critic and 'Current State' going to the imitation reward.

stage4_extra_inputs.what: current normalized exoskeleton torques [u_r, u_l] (2 dims)
stage4_extra_inputs.how: input layer expanded by 2; learned Stage 2 weights kept for the original inputs; weights for the 2 new inputs randomly initialized (scale not reported)
stage4_extra_inputs.source: O p4 and Algorithm 1 lines 23-24 p3; E p4 and Algorithm S1 line 21 p13
stage4_extra_inputs.timing_ambiguity: 'current' torque: this step's exo command (exo acts first) vs the last applied command, not reported

human_actor.outputs: 26 values in [0,1] (13 per side). O p2 calls them 'muscle activations a' and says the policy 'directly controls muscle excitations'; E p2 calls them 'muscle excitations e'.
human_actor.output_distribution: not reported (distribution family, clip vs squash, log-std parameterisation and initial value are all unreported)
human_actor.frozen_in: Stage 3 (O Alg. 1 line 15; E Alg. S1 line 12)
human_actor.frozen_action_mode: not reported (deterministic mean vs stochastic sample while frozen)

exo_actor.inputs: three-step history of bilateral hip flexion angles and angular velocities (12 dims, 4 per timestep) plus a three-step history of its own normalized torque outputs [u_r, u_l] (6 dims, 2 per timestep) (O p2). E p2 adds: 'with no explicit gait-phase or timing variable provided'. E p5 (deployment): 'a three-step history of bilateral hip angles, angular velocities, and its own normalized torque outputs'.
exo_actor.per_timestep_block_assumed: [q_hip_r, q_hip_l, qdot_hip_r, qdot_hip_l] + [u_r, u_l]; the order is not reported
exo_actor.sample_spacing: one control step (20 ms), implied by '4 dims per timestep' and E p5 'At the 50 Hz control rate, the actor consumed the same 18-dimensional observation as in training'; not stated explicitly
exo_actor.window_derived: three consecutive samples span 40 ms oldest-to-newest
exo_actor.includes_current_sample: not reported (kinematics t, t-1, t-2 plausible; own actions are necessarily past actions t-1, t-2, t-3)
exo_actor.observation_normalisation: not reported. omega_s = 2.0 rad/s appears only in the Stage 4 reward (O Eq5 p4; E Eq6 p4), not as an observation scaling.
exo_actor.units: not reported (rad and rad/s plausible; hardware angle = pelvis-femur IMU difference, velocity = thigh gyro minus pelvis gyro about the flexion axis, E p5)
exo_actor.action_stored_in_history: not reported (sampled, mean or clipped action)
exo_actor.filtering: none in training or deployment (E p5: trained on unfiltered kinematics; no online filtering at deployment)
exo_actor.outputs: normalized bilateral hip torque commands u in [-1,1]^2, multiplied by the stage torque limit (O p2; E p2)
exo_actor.initialisation: initialised at start (O Alg. 1 line 2) and re-initialised at the start of Stage 3 (O Alg. 1 line 15; E Alg. S1 line 12)
exo_actor.deployed: Stage 4 exo actor only (O p4; E p5)

critic.architecture: one MLP critic V_psi, hidden sizes [256, 128], shared by both actors
critic.source: O p2, p4; E p2, p4; O Alg. 1; E Alg. S1
critic.inputs: 'the full system state' (O p4; E p4 'sharing a single critic over the full system state'); contents, dimension and any change across stages not reported
critic.continuity_across_stages: initialised once (O Alg. 1 line 2; E Alg. S1 line 1) and updated in every stage; no reset or re-initialisation described
critic.value_heads: not reported (a single V_psi is written; E cites the MADDPG centralised-critic paper [20] for the MARL formulation)
critic.value_target: not reported beyond PPO with GAE (lambda 0.95, gamma 0.99)
critic.reward_to_actor_assignment: not reported explicitly. Table I / Table S2 give ONE weight per term per stage, which reads as a single scalar team reward shared by both actors. O p4 also says stage-specific reward terms 'can be enabled or disabled per agent', which leaves per-agent reward sets possible.
critic.joint_update_form: not reported (one joint PPO ratio over the product policy vs separate clipped losses per actor with a common advantage; one vs several optimizers)

rewards.name: r_fwd
rewards.source: O Eq2a p3, E Eq2a p2; weights O Table I p2, E Table S2 p13

rewards.name: r_qpos (imitation, position)
rewards.equation: r_qpos = dt * sum_{i in J} w_i * exp(-8 * (q_i - q_i_ref)^2)
rewards.stage_note: 1.0* in Stages 3-4: hip imitation zeroed through w_i (E: all hip DOFs; O footnote: hip flexion only). E Table S2 footnote: 'The magnitude of the imitation terms is carried by the per-joint weights in Table S3.'
rewards.source: O Eq2c p3, E Eq2b p2; O Table I, E Tables S2-S3

rewards.name: r_qvel (imitation, velocity)
rewards.equation: r_qvel = dt * sum_{i in J} w_i * exp(-8 * (qdot_i - rho * qdot_i_ref)^2), rho = v_star / qdot_pelvis_ref(t)

symbols.rho: time-dependent scaling of reference joint velocities to the target speed (written with (t))
symbols.qdot_pelvis_ref(t): reference forward pelvis velocity at time t

rewards.stage_note: as r_qpos; reference positions are NOT rescaled, only velocities
rewards.derived_note: for pelvis_tx the scaled reference velocity equals v_star at every t, so the pelvis_tx velocity term (w = 0.80 / 0.40) acts as a second forward-speed term with kernel exp(-8 (v - 1.25)^2)
rewards.source: O Eq2d p3, E Eq2c p2

rewards.name: r_muscle
rewards.source: O Eq2b p3, E Eq3a p2

rewards.name: r_delta_a (activation smoothness bonus)
rewards.note: a positive bonus, maximal (= dt) when activations do not change; E p2 describes it as 'penalizing ... its rate of change'
rewards.source: O Eq2e p3, E Eq3b p2

rewards.name: r_hip_act

symbols.M_hip: O p3: 'includes iliopsoas, gluteus maximus, rectus femoris, and hamstrings on both legs'; E p3: 'comprises major hip flexors and extensors such as the iliopsoas, gluteus maximus, rectus femoris, and hamstrings on both legs'

rewards.note: the muscles in this reward are exactly the four groups whose right-side activation reduction is the O headline (10.1%)
rewards.source: O Eq3 p3, E Eq4 p3

rewards.name: r_exo (Stage 3 form)
rewards.equation: r_exo3 = dt * sum_{j in {l,r}} alpha_d * u_j^2 * sign(u_j * omega_j)
rewards.source: O Eq4 p3, E Eq5 p3; weight row 'r_exo' in O Table I / E Table S2 denotes Eq4 in Stage 3

rewards.name: r_exo (Stage 4 form)
rewards.equation: r_exo4 = dt * sum_{j in {l,r}} ( alpha * u_j * omega_hat_j - beta * u_j^2 - lambda_s * max(0, |u_j| - delta)^2 ), omega_hat_j = clip(omega_j / omega_s, -1, 1)
rewards.derived_optimum: per joint, instantaneous: u* = omega_hat for |omega_hat| <= 0.8; u* = sign(omega_hat) * (0.3 |omega_hat| + 3.2) / 4.3 above (u* = 0.814 at |omega_hat| = 1). Numerically verified.
rewards.source: O Eq5 p4, E Eq6 p4; same weight row denotes Eq5 in Stage 4

rewards.name: r_delta_tau (torque-rate penalty)
rewards.source: O Eq6 p4, E Eq7 p4

rewards.name: total reward
rewards.equation: Stage 1 (O Eq1 p3; E Eq1 p2): r1 = w_fwd r_fwd + w_mus r_muscle + w_qpos r_qpos + w_qvel r_qvel + w_da r_delta_a. Stages 2-4: weighted sum of the active terms with Table I / S2 weights (no explicit equation printed).
rewards.note: Stage 2 uses 'the same reward in Eqs. (1) and (2)' (O p3) / 'the same Stage 1 reward, Eqs. (1), (2), and (3)' (E p3). Inactive terms marked '-' in the tables are null here.
rewards.source: O p3, Table I; E p2-3, Table S2

imitation_weights.source: E Table S3 p14 (bilateral DOFs use identical left/right weights and are listed once; '-' = not tracked in that term; pelvis translation along x/z tracked in velocity only)

weight_sums_derived.note: bilateral DOFs counted on both sides

imitation_weights.O_variant: O Table I footnote p2: 'Hip flexion imitation weights are set to zero in Stages 3 and 4 while other joint imitation terms remain active.' O prints no per-joint table. If reproducing O literally, hip_adduction and hip_rotation would keep their Stage 1-2 weights (0.05/0.03 and 0.03/0.02) in Stages 3-4; this is a sweep option, E Table S3 is the default.
imitation_weights.stage_group_note: Table S3 has only two columns per term (Stages 1-2, Stages 3-4); Stage 3 and Stage 4 share the same imitation weights. The non-hip weights also change at Stage 3 (e.g., pelvis_tilt qpos 0.20->0.40, knee qpos 0.20->0.30, pelvis_tx qvel 0.80->0.40, mtp qvel 0.01->0.00).

ppo_by_stage.source: O Table II p4 = E Table S4 p14 ('Values are shared across stages unless noted otherwise')
ppo_by_stage.derived_per_update: 32 envs x 2048 = 65,536 transitions per update; 4 minibatches of 16,384 per epoch; up to 80 gradient steps per update (fewer if target-KL early stopping triggers)
ppo_by_stage.hyperparameter_names_note: the parameter set (n_steps per env, batch_size, n_epochs, target_kl, max_grad_norm, ent_coef, n_envs) matches Stable-Baselines3 PPO naming; SB3 use is not stated in either paper
not_reported: action distribution, log-std init and whether log-std is state dependent
whether actors and critic share one optimizer or one learning rate
total wall-clock per stage (only 28 h / 100M overall rate)
ppo_by_stage.throughput_reported: all training on an Intel Xeon W-2145 (3.70 GHz, 8-core), approximately 28 h per 100 M simulation steps (O p4; E p4)

stages.name: Human baseline gait learning (human only)
stages.exo_actor: initialised (O Alg. 1 line 2) but not used
stages.steps: approximately 320 M simulation steps ('converging over approximately 320 M', O p5; E p6); counting unit not stated
stages.transition_rule: start from random pi_h, pi_e, V_psi; end: save pi_h(1). Stopping rule: not reported beyond 'converging'.
stages.source: O p2-3, Alg. 1 lines 1-7, Tables I-II; E p2, Alg. S1 lines 1-5, Tables S2-S4

stages.name: Human adaptation to the added (passive) exoskeleton mass
stages.exo_actor: present but its output has no effect (torque limit 0)
stages.steps: approximately 160 M ('convergence is reached within approximately 160 M steps ... roughly half the steps required in Stage 1', O p5; E p6)
stages.rewards_active: identical to Stage 1 (O p3; E p3)
stages.transition_rule: load pi_h(1); attach device; set exo torque to zero; critic continues (no reset described); optimizer, log-std and normalisation carry-over not reported; end: save pi_h(2)
stages.figure_note: read from Fig. 2 (O p5), approximate: Stage 2 episode reward starts near the bottom of the axis (about 0-1) rather than at the Stage 1 plateau (about 6.5) and climbs back to about 6.8 by 160 M; i.e., attaching the device initially degrades the Stage 1 policy substantially, or the logger/episode setup differs
stages.source: O p3, p5, Alg. 1 lines 8-13; E p3, p6, Alg. S1 lines 6-11

stages.name: Assistance-timing learning with frozen human
stages.steps: approximately 1.1 M ('Stage 3 establishes an initial flexion-assist timing pattern in approximately 1.1 M simulation steps', O p5; E p6)

rewards_active.imitation: 1.0 with Table S3 Stage 3-4 weights (hip DOFs zero)

stages.transition_rule: set tau_max = 6 Nm; freeze pi_h(2); re-initialise pi_e; disable hip imitation; add r_hip_act and r_exo3 (Algorithms). The re-weighting of r_fwd/r_muscle/r_delta_a and activation of r_constraint/r_foot appear only in Table I/S2. End: save pi_e(3).
stages.rationale_argued: freezing removes non-stationarity; 6 Nm constrains destabilising exploration; hip imitation disabled 'to prevent the exoskeleton from exploiting tracking rewards by resisting hip motion change' (O p3, O p7)
stages.source: O p3, p5, p7, Alg. 1 lines 14-20; E p3, p6, Alg. S1 lines 12-18

stages.name: Human-exoskeleton co-adaptation
stages.steps: approximately 66 M ('Stage 4 refines this through full co-adaptation over approximately 66 M steps', O p5; E p6)

rewards_active.imitation: 1.0 with Table S3 Stage 3-4 weights (hip DOFs zero)

stages.transition_rule: set tau_max = 25 Nm; load pi_e(3); unfreeze pi_h(2); augment human observation with current [u_r, u_l]; expand human input by 2 (copy existing weights, random init for new); replace r_exo3 by r_exo4; add r_delta_tau; r_hip_act 2.0 -> 5.0 (table only). Joint PPO update of (pi_h, pi_e, V_psi).
stages.output: final co-adapted policies; the Stage 4 exo actor is the deployed controller
stages.source: O p3-4, p5, Alg. 1 lines 21-28; E p3-4, p6, Alg. S1 lines 19-25

evaluation_metrics.name: stage1_bilateral_symmetry_pearson_r
evaluation_metrics.definition_as_published: O p5: 'The learned gait shows strong bilateral symmetry across all joints (Pearson r > 0.92)'. E p6: 'strongly symmetric joint kinematics (Pearson r > 0.92)'. It is LEFT-vs-RIGHT symmetry across ALL joints, not a hip-only metric and not a correlation with the reference motion.
evaluation_metrics.source: O p5, Fig. 2 p5 (hip, knee, ankle, right solid vs left dashed, mean +/- 1 s.d. over normalized gait cycle); E p6
ambiguities: which joints ('all joints'; Fig. 2 shows hip, knee, ankle)
computed on per-limb gait-cycle-normalized mean curves (each limb normalized to its own cycle, as Fig. 2 overlays them) vs raw time series
number of cycles/episodes, deterministic vs stochastic policy
Pearson r is insensitive to amplitude scaling and offsets
evaluation_metrics.tolerance_basis: published only as a bound; no seed spread reported. Proposal (not published): per-joint left-right Pearson r >= 0.92 for hip, knee and ankle on every seed, plus an additional (unpublished) correlation-and-RMSE check against the reference trajectory because symmetry alone can pass an abnormal gait.

evaluation_metrics.name: stage1_toe_off_percent_gait_cycle
evaluation_metrics.definition_as_published: toe-off timing as % of the gait cycle; O p5: '57.8 +/- 1.1% (right) and 58.5 +/- 0.9% (left) of the gait cycle, consistent with physiological norms for treadmill walking [16]'
evaluation_metrics.published_value: right 57.8%, left 58.5% (O); E p6 reports a single '57.8 +/- 1.1%'
evaluation_metrics.uncertainty: +/-1.1 (right), +/-0.9 (left); dispersion measure and population (SD across gait cycles presumably) not stated
evaluation_metrics.source: O p5; E p6; vertical lines in O Fig. 2 p5
ambiguities: gait-cycle origin (heel strike assumed; hardware analyses use peak hip flexion instead)
event detection method and force threshold
cycles pooled across episodes/seeds
stochastic vs deterministic evaluation
evaluation_metrics.tolerance_basis: the published +/- is cycle-to-cycle spread, not seed spread. Proposal (not published): seed-mean toe-off within 55-61% on both sides and |right - left| <= 2 percentage points.

evaluation_metrics.name: stage2_trajectory_rmse_deg
evaluation_metrics.definition_as_published: O p5: 'Joint trajectories are well preserved (RMSE < 3.6 deg for all joints; Pearson r > 0.92 across all joint pairs), and bilateral symmetry is maintained'. E p6: 'preserving the learned trajectories (RMSE < 3.6 deg across all joints) and bilateral symmetry'.
evaluation_metrics.source: O p5; E p6; Fig. 2 right column
ambiguities: comparator: Stage 2 vs Stage 1 trajectories (E wording 'preserving the learned trajectories' implies this) vs the reference motion
which joints ('all joints')
RMSE of gait-cycle-normalized means vs pooled samples
O's 'Pearson r > 0.92 across all joint pairs': Stage1-Stage2 pairs or left-right pairs
evaluation_metrics.tolerance_basis: use the published bound directly: RMSE(Stage 2 mean vs Stage 1 mean, same seed) <= 3.6 deg for hip, knee and ankle, both sides; also report pelvis DOFs.

evaluation_metrics.name: stage_budgets_to_convergence
evaluation_metrics.definition_as_published: approximate simulation steps per stage: S1 ~320 M, S2 ~160 M, S3 ~1.1 M, S4 ~66 M
evaluation_metrics.published_value: 320 M / 160 M / 1.1 M / 66 M (sum 547.1 M, derived)
evaluation_metrics.source: O p5 and Fig. 2 (x-axes 0-320 M and 0-160 M); Fig. 3a x-axis 'Timesteps (x10^6)' about 0-65; E p6
ambiguities: aggregate over 32 envs vs per env (32x difference)
whether 'simulation steps' are control steps (50 Hz) or physics steps
convergence criterion
evaluation_metrics.tolerance_basis: budgets are inputs, not outcomes; run the published budgets under the declared counting convention and sweep the alternative for S3/S4.

evaluation_metrics.name: stage4_exo_power_reward_trend
evaluation_metrics.definition_as_published: O p5: 'the exoskeleton assistance power reward increases from -0.12 to 0.08 and the hip muscle activation penalty decreases in magnitude over the course of training' (Fig. 3a, left axis green = exo assistance power reward, right axis red dashed = hip muscle activation penalty)
ambiguities: logging unit: per-step vs per-episode, with or without dt, with or without the 4.0 weight
derived: per-step unweighted bracket sum without dt is consistent with the numbers (u ~ omega_hat and RMS hip velocity ~1 rad/s gives ~0.08; a saturated Stage 3 policy gives roughly -0.1 to -0.2)
right-axis penalty values not legible in the render
evaluation_metrics.tolerance_basis: soft check only (sign change from negative to positive), because the unit is unknown.

evaluation_metrics.name: stage4_peak_normalized_torque
evaluation_metrics.definition_as_published: peak of the normalized exo torque u (torque / tau_max) over the gait cycle; O p5: 'peak normalized torque of 0.83 occurring at 75% of the gait cycle during the late-swing flexion phase'; Fig. 3c is a bilateral average with +/-1 SD
evaluation_metrics.published_value: 0.83 at 75% gait cycle (O p5, E p6, E p7); 0.84 in O p6 ablation text
evaluation_metrics.source: O p5 Fig. 3c; O p6; E p6-7
ambiguities: peak of the bilateral mean profile vs mean of per-cycle peaks
deterministic vs stochastic actions
gait-cycle origin (heel strike assumed)
evaluation_metrics.derived_note: the reward-optimal value at saturated hip velocity is 0.814, so a peak of about 0.81-0.83 is predicted by r_exo4 alone whenever peak |omega| >= 1.6 rad/s; this metric cannot discriminate SMAT from a velocity-proportional controller
evaluation_metrics.tolerance_basis: Proposal (not published): 0.83 +/- 0.08 on each seed, AND report the same metric for the matched velocity baselines.

evaluation_metrics.name: stage4_negative_power_time_fraction
evaluation_metrics.definition_as_published: O p5: 'the negative-work time fraction (fraction of the gait cycle where P = tau * qdot < 0) to 10%, as reflected in Fig. 3d'. E p6: 'confines negative work to only 10% of the cycle in simulation (the portion where P = tau * qdot < 0)'.
ambiguities: computed on the bilateral-average profile (Fig. 3d) or per sample pooled over cycles/sides
tau = applied torque (tau_max * u) and qdot = hip flexion velocity (assumed)
it is a TIME fraction, not the energy ratio R_pos used on hardware
evaluation_metrics.tolerance_basis: Proposal (not published): <= 15% per seed (published has no spread); report exact definition used.

evaluation_metrics.name: stage4_vs_stage2_right_hip_activation_reduction
evaluation_metrics.definition_as_published: O p6: 'comparing right-side activation between Stage 2 (no assistive torque) and Stage 4 (maximum assistive torque, tau_max = 25 Nm). All four muscles show reduced mean activation with exoskeleton assistance, averaging 10.1% across muscles. ... rectus femoris (-13.5%) and iliopsoas (-10.5%) ... Hamstrings decrease by 9.7% and gluteus maximus by 6.6%'
evaluation_metrics.published_value: RF -13.5%, iliopsoas -10.5%, hamstrings -9.7%, gluteus maximus -6.6%; mean 10.1% (simple mean = 10.075, derived)
evaluation_metrics.uncertainty: not reported (Fig. 4 bands are +/-1 s.d. across cycles)
evaluation_metrics.source: O p6 text and Fig. 4 (right side, Stage 2 blue vs Stage 4 orange, dashed toe-off per condition); restated E p2
evaluation_metrics.same_device_mass: yes: both Stage 2 and Stage 4 have the device attached (Stage 2 zero torque, Stage 4 25 Nm)

ablations.name: Stage 3 only
ablations.definition: Stage 3 exo policy without Stage 4 co-adaptation

ablations.figure_read: Fig. 5 (O p6 dashed green; E p7 purple), approximate: about -1 from 0 to ~45%, switching to +1 around 50-55%, +1 until ~85%, back toward -1 near 95-100%
ablations.derived_note: this is the optimum of r_exo3 (bang-bang sign(omega)), so the outcome is predicted by the Stage 3 reward itself
ablations.source: O p6 Fig. 5; E p6-7 Fig. 5

ablations.name: Stage 4 only (from Stage 2, no Stage 3)
ablations.definition: Stage 4 training initialised from the Stage 2 human with a randomly initialised exo actor, full Stage 4 reward including r_exo4
ablations.initialisation: pi_h(2), random pi_e (O Fig. 5 caption; O p7 'Stage 4 begins from a randomly initialized exoskeleton policy')
ablations.runs: 3 (O Fig. 5 caption: 'dashed red, mean across three runs'); E caption does not state
ablations.published_outcome: collapse to near-zero output: peak normalized torque 0.14 vs 0.84 (O) / 0.83 (E), an 83% reduction; the minimal torque opposes joint motion over 32% of the cycle (vs 10% in full SMAT)
ablations.authors_explanation_argued: 'the second term of (5) rewards minimising torque magnitude, so the policy discovers that producing no torque maximises that reward component' (O p6; E p7)
ablations.derived_note: d r_exo4 / du at u = 0 equals 0.3 * omega_hat, not zero; the full r_exo4 is maximised at u = omega_hat. The stated mechanism therefore does not by itself explain the collapse; exploration-noise costs (beta u^2, lambda_s, r_delta_tau under a noisy random policy), critic bias after the reward switch, or human-side terms are untested alternatives.
ablations.source: O p6 Fig. 5, O p7; E p6-7 Fig. 5

common.power_analysis: P = commanded torque x angular velocity after One-Euro filtering (offline analysis); gait cycles segmented at peak hip flexion because there are no ground-reaction-force sensors
common.source: O Table III p4, O p4-5; E Table I p4, E p4-6

O_2026_03.compute: Raspberry Pi 4B mounted on the frame
O_2026_03.fitting: exo hip axis aligned with the anatomical hip axis per subject
O_2026_03.protocol: 5 healthy participants; fixed order: 5 min familiarisation, 5 min no-assist (worn, zero command, back-drivable), 5 min at 10 Nm, 5 min at 15 Nm; 2 min rests; 1.25 m/s treadmill
O_2026_03.limitations_stated: encoder angles may overestimate biological hip motion due to soft tissue and strap looseness; velocity noisier than motion capture (O p7)

E_2026_08.compute: Raspberry Pi 5 (no deterministic real-time scheduling; 50 Hz chosen for timing reliability and CAN utilisation)
E_2026_08.sensing: 3 x LPMS-B2 IMUs (LP-Research) on pelvis and both thighs via BLE; hip angle = pelvis-femur difference; hip angular velocity = thigh gyro minus pelvis gyro about the flexion axis; IMUs zeroed in standing before each trial; encoders available but IMUs used
E_2026_08.loop: fixed 20 ms period, command transmitted at end of cycle, idle until next; no timing overruns noted
E_2026_08.torque_scale_Nm: 15 for SMAT (about 12 Nm peak); Ctrl-B commanded at 12 Nm
E_2026_08.mechanics: adjustable waist width, adjustable thigh-link length, anteroposterior slide of lateral extensions, vertical vest height; carbon-fibre back plate; passive abd/add hinge between waist frame and actuator assembly; fitted once per participant
E_2026_08.protocol: 8 adults; familiarisation 5 min unpowered + 10 min SMAT; order: standing rest, No-Exo, Passive, {SMAT, Ctrl-B} randomised, Passive, No-Exo, standing rest; ~6 min trials, last 2 min averaged; >= 5 min seated rest; 1.25 m/s; COSMED K5
E_2026_08.source: E p4-6, Table I, Fig. 1, Fig. 3

derived_analysis.label: derived by us from the published equations; not claims made by the authors
derived_analysis.reward_optimal_exo_policy: per joint, ignoring human-side effects: maximise 0.3*u*w - 0.15*u^2 - 2*max(0,|u|-0.8)^2 with w = clip(omega/2, -1, 1). Solution u*(w) = w for |w| <= 0.8, sign(w)*(0.3|w| + 3.2)/4.3 for |w| > 0.8; u*(1) = 0.814. Verified by grid search.
derived_analysis.rate_penalty_filter: inside |u| <= 0.8 and with the Stage 4 weights (r_exo 4.0, r_delta_tau 1.0) the exo-only per-step objective is -0.6*(u_t - w_t)^2 - 1.0*(u_t - u_{t-1})^2 + const. The discounted LQ solution (gamma 0.99, w held constant) is u_t = 0.529*w_t + 0.471*u_{t-1} (pole 0.471, time constant about 27 ms, about 2.4% of a 1.1 s stride); the myopic solution has pole 0.625 (about 43 ms).
derived_analysis.stage3_optimum: r_exo3 = 0.5*u^2*sign(u*omega) is maximised by u = sign(omega) with |u| = 1 (bang-bang), which is exactly the published 'Stage 3 only' saturation and abrupt reversal
predictions_from_reward_alone: peak normalized torque about 0.81 whenever peak |omega| exceeds about 1.6 rad/s (published sim 0.83; hardware 8.1/10 = 0.81, 12.2/15 = 0.81, 12.39/15 = 0.83; offline 0.77-0.82)
power tau*omega is nonnegative except where the filtered command lags velocity zero crossings, so a small negative-power time fraction and R_pos near 1 are expected
peak torque nearly speed-invariant once |omega| saturates (offline 11.6-12.3 Nm across 0.6-1.8 m/s)
positive power rising with speed (hardware 11.6 -> 17.8 -> 21.5 W)
a lag relative to the biological hip moment, because hip flexion velocity peaks after the flexion moment
mandatory_baselines: B0 reward-matched no-assist control: continue the Stage 2 human under the full Stage 4 human reward (r_muscle 0.15, r_hip_act 5.0, hip imitation off, r_fwd 1.5, constraint/foot terms) for the same 66 M steps with tau_max = 0; compare its activations with Stage 2 and with SMAT Stage 4
B1 u = u*(omega_hat) (instantaneous reward-optimal), tau_max 25 Nm, human co-adapted under the Stage 4 reward at the same budget
B2 B1 passed through the LQ filter u_t = 0.529*u*(w_t) + 0.471*u_{t-1} (rate-limited velocity controller)
B3 gain sweep u = clip(k*omega_hat, -0.8, 0.8), k in {0.5, 1, 2}, plus a one-step (20 ms) delay variant for hardware parity
B4 phase-based fixed profile (e.g., shaped like the published SMAT mean profile, or a hip flexion/extension profile) at matched RMS and peak torque
B5 unstaged simultaneous two-actor PPO from Stage 2 at matched total budget, with and without a behaviour-cloned u = w warm start (tests whether Stage 3 matters beyond initialisation)
derived_analysis.fig_scale_checks: Fig. 3a -0.12 -> 0.08 is consistent with per-step, unweighted, un-dt-scaled bracket sums of r_exo4 over both hips when u follows omega_hat with RMS hip velocity about 1 rad/s; Fig. 2 episode reward plateau about 6.5-7 bounds episode length from below (see simulator)
derived_analysis.throughput: 28 h / 100 M on 8 cores = 992 aggregate steps/s = 124 steps/s per core = 31 steps/s per env (32 envs). Per-env counting would require about 31,700 aggregate steps/s on 8 cores, which is implausible for a Python-driven 26-muscle MuJoCo env with PPO updates, so aggregate counting is the more likely reading (argued, not stated). Full pipeline 547.1 M = 153 h at their rate; Stages 3+4 (67.1 M) = 18.8 h; Stages 1+2 (480 M) = 134 h.

gate_tolerance_basis.label: facts that constrain tolerance setting; the proposals are ours, not published, and must be frozen before any Stage 4 result is seen
facts: No simulated number in either paper carries a seed-level uncertainty; the only +/- values are cycle-to-cycle spreads (toe-off +/-1.1 / +/-0.9%) and Fig. 3/4 bands (+/-1 SD over cycles).
Only one simulated condition reports multiple runs: 'Stage 4 only', mean of three runs (O Fig. 5 caption).
Three published targets are bounds, not point values: symmetry r > 0.92, Stage 2 RMSE < 3.6 deg (and O's r > 0.92).

Peak normalized torque (0.83; 0.84 once) sits next to the reward optimum 0.814, and the negative-power fraction (10%) and R_pos are largely implied by r_exo4; gates on them test implementation fidelity, not the SMAT mechanism.
The 10.1% activation reduction is a mean of four relative reductions (13.5, 10.5, 9.7, 6.6; simple mean 10.075); 6.1% is a different aggregation (six groups, both legs).
The Stage 2 comparator for activation reductions is confounded by reward changes; a reproduction that matches 10.1% without B0 does not reproduce a device effect.

proposals.L1_symmetry: per-joint L-R Pearson r >= 0.92 (hip, knee, ankle) on >= 3 seeds, plus declared reference-tracking RMSE reported
proposals.L2_rmse: Stage 2 vs Stage 1 mean trajectories <= 3.6 deg per joint (bound as published)
proposals.L3_activation_4group_right: all four groups reduced on every seed; seed mean within 10.1 +/- 5 points; reported beside B0 and B1-B3
proposals.L3_activation_6group_bilateral: 6.1 +/- 4 points with the averaging declared in advance
proposals.L3_ablations_direction: Stage 4 only: peak <= 0.3 and opposing-power time >= 20%; Stage 4 only w/o r_exo4: mean torque in extension during swing and negative-power time >= 25%; Stage 3 only: |u| >= 0.95 for >= 50% of the cycle; each on >= 3 seeds
proposals.offline_replay: peak 10.5-13.5 Nm at 15 Nm scale on all three speeds; lag 5-25% of the cycle; report the same for B1-B3
